Each element is built from the rest of HextaUI. Code fences become Code Blocks, GitHub callouts like [!NOTE] use Alert, task lists use read-only Checkboxes, and tables scroll sideways with a menu to copy them as Markdown or CSV. Pass sources and [1] becomes a citation chip, while marks inside code are left alone.
External links say “opens in a new tab”, citation chips are named after their source, and heading anchors are named “Link to …”.

Headings get ids from their text, with an optional link icon to share them. Images load lazily with a placeholder and caption, footnotes link back to their mark, external links open in a new tab and say so, and text direction is detected per block. It works as well for READMEs and changelogs as for streamed answers.
Images keep their alt text, and tables keep their header cells for screen reader navigation.
Markdown made for AI answers. It streams smoothly and never shows half-typed syntax, with headings you can link to, tables you can copy as Markdown or CSV…

Models answer in Markdown, and they write it a token at a time. A plain renderer flashes raw asterisks, half-built tables and unclosed code fences while it streams. Markdown completes unfinished syntax as it goes and paces the text like the Streaming block, so formatting appears in place.
